<-*Dell'origine della Virtù.*->

**XL.** La virtù tiene la proprietà d'essere d'origine divina (1); conciossiachè queste tre sue parti tutte insieme costituiscono la vera virtù; e ciascuna di esse si trova sempre colle altre due congiunta. E in effetti nella prudenza avvi ancora la fortezza, in quantochè la mente nel ricercare il vero vi si travaglia e dura fatica, nè si ristà sino a che nol ritrovi; vi è anche la temperanza, essendo che è pur cosa savia l'ignorare talune cose. Nella temperanza poi si ritrova la prudenza, che ci consiglia a non trasandare le cose utili alla vita, per non riportarne detrimento; e perciò la Medicina è di origine divina, perchè dettata da questo vero eterno: vi è anche la fortezza, acciocchè sappia egli tenersi lungi dai piaceri. Infine nella fortezza si trova pure la prudenza per difendere l'onesto; vi è poi la temperanza, acciocchè i vincitori non vogliano distruggere i vinti, che possono senza danno serbare in vita.

<-*Della virtù vera.*->

**XLI.** Non avvi adunque virtù alcuna che stia sola, chè ove trovi veramente la virtù, sii certo che vi si trovano tutte le altre insieme riunite: poichè le virtù, che stiano isolate, meritano appena, secondo le parole di S. Agostino, il nome di virtù (2).

<-*Della Grazia divina.*->

**XLII.** Quella virtù poi, che sola dee dirsi vera, e come tale va innanzi a

(1) Cap. III.
(2) Epist. CLXVI; altrimenti XXIX ad Hieronymum, c. 3, n. 11, cap. 4, n. 14.

---

<-*Virtutis divinae origo.*->

**XL.** Virtus divinae originis proprietatem obtinet (1); namque hae tres ejus partes una sunt vera virtus; et quaeque earum semper est cum aliis duabus complicata. Etenim in prudentia et fortitudo inest, ut in vero vestigando laboret, nec in eo nisi explorato acquiescat; inest et temperantia, qua quaedam ignorare sapientia est. In temperantia et prudentia inest, ne quis ad exitium usque sui utilibus vitae rebus abstineat: quare Medicinae origo divina; nam ab hoc vero aeterno dictata: inest et fortitudo, ut sustineat a voluptatibus temperare. In fortitudine et prudentia inest, ut pro honesto pugnet; inest et temperantia, qua victores nolint perdere, quos possunt servare victus.

<-*Virtus vera.*->

**XLI.** Igitur nulla virtus solitaria, et ubi ex vero una ibi omnes Comites adsunt: solae enim virtutes vix est, ut cum Divo Augustino (2) loquar, ut nomen virtutum mereantur.

<-*Divina gratia.*->

**XLII.** Virtus autem, quae una vera, et quia vera, omnes virtutes praestat, non

(1) De qua Cap. III.
(2) Epistola CLXVII; alias XXIX, ad Hieronymum, cap. 3, n. 11, et cap. 4, n. 14, T. II in Edit. Paris.

### Della Virtù degli Stoici; e della Virtù Cristiana.

XXXVIII. Questa forza del vero, che raffrena gli affetti , ma che però non basta a temperare la ferocia , da cui essi pullulano , è la *Virtù morale imperfetta*, come S. Agostino vuole che sia quella degli Etnici (1). La forza del vero, che pugna contro la cupidità , e contro l’ *amor di sè* che la partorisce, è la *Virtù Etica Cristiana*, mercè la quale l’uomo trasmuta ciò che più alletta l’animo in dispregio ed abbiezione di sè stesso, ed è detto *Umiltà*, base e principio di tutte le virtù Cristiane.

### Tre parti della Virtù.

XXXIX. ...oratory, and the art of poetry, then it must properly be called Wisdom. This force of truth, with which the passions are restrained, constitutes *Ethical Virtue*, or the virtue of action, which is called *Moral*.

### Of the Virtue of the Stoics; and of Christian Virtue.

XXXVIII. This force of the truth, which restrains the passions but which is not enough to temper the ferocity from which they spring, is *imperfect moral virtue*, such as St. Augustine considers to be that of the Heathens <note>original: "Ethnicorum"</note> (1). The force of the truth, which fights against cupidity and against the *self-love* <note>original: "amor di sè"</note> that gives birth to it, is *Christian Ethical Virtue*, by means of which man transforms that which most allures the soul into contempt and abjection of himself, and this is called *Humility*, the base and principle of all Christian virtues.

### Three parts of Virtue.

XXXIX. When the mind is moved by virtue to labor in the search for truth, and will not rest until it is attained, it is called *Prudence*: if the soul, by means of virtue, knows how to keep itself far from the unbridled nature of the senses, one then has *Temperance*: if the affections of the soul find themselves sustained by virtue and free from fear, one will have *Fortitude*.
auditTranslation:
->*Of the origin of Virtue.*<-

**XL.** Virtue possesses the property of being of divine origin (1); for these three parts of it together constitute true virtue; and each of them is always found joined with the other two. Indeed, in prudence there is also fortitude, in that the mind, in searching for the truth, labors and endures fatigue, and does not rest until it finds it; there is also temperance, since it is a wise thing to be ignorant of certain things. In temperance, then, one finds prudence, which counsels us not to neglect things useful to life, so as not to suffer detriment; and therefore Medicine is of divine origin, because it was dictated by this eternal truth: there is also fortitude, so that one may know how to keep oneself far from pleasures. Finally, in fortitude, one also finds prudence to defend the honest; there is also temperance, so that the victors do not wish to destroy the vanquished whom they can keep alive without harm.

->*Of true virtue.*<-

**XLI.** There is, therefore, no virtue that stands alone, for where you truly find virtue, be certain that all the others are found united with it: since virtues that stand in isolation scarcely deserve, in the words of St. Augustine, the name of virtue (2).

->*Of divine Grace.*<-

**XLII.** That virtue, however, which alone must be called true, and as such goes before all others, is not proper to man, but rather belongs to God, and is called *Divine Grace*, which, by means of its light, makes it clearly seen by Christians what their duty is in this life; and it operates in such a way that with a single species of irremovable assent we assent both to the rational order, upon which our contemplation must dwell, and to the order of the facts that must be performed.
And in this way the principles of *Christian Morality* are considered demonstrated.

such that the Master turned toward me
saying: "Do not doubt while I lead you."
"Glory to God in the highest" <note>original: "Gloria in excelsis deo"</note> they all
were saying, from what I understood nearby,
from where the cry could be heard.

Where the sun turned as its homeland: so that it moved no more. And he bound it with Gyaros and Mykonos, neighboring islands. The truth they wish it to be is that this island was often shaken by earthquakes. Wherefore the inhabitants went to the oracle of Apollo to ask for a remedy. And he commanded that certain sacrifices be made: and for the future, the dead should not be buried there. Therefore Apollo made it immobile: and that he bound it to Gyaros and Mykonos signifies that the men of those islands inhabited it. It was called first Asteria: afterwards Delos. Which in Greek signifies "clear" and "manifest": because returning to the surface it became manifest: or rather because Apollo gave manifest answers there. **SUCH THAT THE MASTER** turned toward me. **THEN BEGAN** from all sides a cry: Dante felt the mountain shake: and after such shaking he heard that all the spirits of that place with one voice sang: "Glory to God in the highest" <note>original: "Gloria in excelsis deo"</note>: which song the Church uses when with joy and gladness we return thanks to God. This hymn was sung by the angels at the birth of the Savior.

We remained immobile and in suspense
like the shepherds who first heard that song
until the trembling ceased and it was finished.
Then we resumed our holy path,
watching the shadows that lay upon the ground,
returned already to their accustomed weeping.
No ignorance ever with such great war
made me desirous of knowing,
if my memory does not err in this,
as it seemed to me then, thinking upon it;
nor because of the haste was I daring to ask,
nor could I see anything by myself.
Thus I went on, timid and pensive.

...to understand. **THERE.** i.e., in that place. It is easy for anyone in whom there is at least mediocre talent to notice how much this place requires that many and various things be said in detestation of avarice. Because if we could free human minds from such a pernicious disease, the life of mortals would be too happy: and all domestic and civil dissension would cease, as would every foreign war. Nor would we take up many laborious cares, all useless to us, which strip us of honor and peace, and deprive us of that leisure <note>term: "ocio" - referring here to the classical ideal of productive, contemplative rest.</note> which we could spend on things pertaining to our salvation. But if we collect what has been said in various places of this volume, perhaps the listener will feel partly satisfied.

<column-break/>

...they strove to overcome, i.e., to conquer the road, i.e., to pass it. When Dante felt such trembling in the mountain as usually happens with a thing that is about to fall, which first trembles and then drops. And he uses this comparison: that Delos did not shake so strongly when it was moved by earthquakes, before Latona—mother of Apollo and Diana, i.e., of the sun and the moon—gave birth there to the two eyes of heaven. Because the moon and the sun are like two eyes of heaven. Delos is one of the Cyclades islands, of which there is such a fable: Jove loved Asteria; she fled him, and obtained from the gods to be transformed into a quail. But Jove, wanting her to cross the sea, changed her into stone: whence she fell into the water and went to the bottom, where she stayed for a long time. Afterwards Jove, at the prayers of Latona his sister <note>In classical mythology, Latona (Leto) was a lover of Jupiter, not his sister.</note>, who conceived Phoebus and Diana by him, brought her back to the surface and made her an island, but a mobile one. In this island Latona gave birth to the sun and the moon.

<image-desc>A decorative blue drop-cap 'N' featuring white scrollwork and floral motifs.</image-desc> **We remained immobile:** we stayed without going any further. **AND IN SUSPENSE:** doubtful in mind. **LIKE THE SHEPHERDS** who first heard: thus we were stupefied; as were the shepherds to whom the angels, singing this canticle, announced that Christ was born. Whence they, descending from the mountains, heard him in the manger between the ox and the ass. **UNTIL THE TREMBLING CEASED:** until the shaking of the mountain stopped. **AND THAT finished:** and until that whole song was completed. Then we resumed our way, and the souls returned to their accustomed weeping. **NO IGNORANCE** ever [put] so much war: because naturally every man desires to know; it happens that ignorance of a thing, i.e., not knowing it, makes war on man: because it goads him and fights him to seek to know it. I did not dare ask Virgil, nor by myself could I...

<summary>This page depicts a sudden, terrifying earthquake on the mountain of Purgatory followed by the souls singing the "Gloria," which Dante compares to the shepherds at the Nativity. Landino’s commentary explains the earthquake through the Greek myth of Delos and provides a moral reflection on how greed destroys social peace.</summary>
<keywords>Dante Alighieri, Purgatorio, Canto XX, Delos, Latona, Apollo, Diana, Avarice, Gloria in excelsis deo, Nativity, Cristoforo Landino</keywords>

<meta>This page follows the dramatic earthquake and the collective singing of the "Gloria" by the souls on the terrace of Avarice. We now transition from the physical manifestation of the mountain’s joy to the arrival of a new companion, the poet Statius, who will explain these phenomena.</meta>

# CANTO XXI OF THE SECOND CANTICLE BY DANTE.

### THE NOBLE SUBJECT MATTER: and nobly treated in this twenty-first canto. In which he sets forth: how as they follow their path they were joined by a soul, from whom they learned the cause of the shaking of the mountain and of the song of the souls. And finally they recognized this man to have been a poet; nor without the greatest pleasure did Virgil recognize him.

<column-break/>

<image-desc>A large historiated initial 'L' containing a scene with two figures in a landscape, representing the meeting of Dante and Virgil with the spirit of Statius. The initial is framed in a square border with decorative elements.</image-desc>

The natural thirst that is never satisfied
except with the water for which the young 
Samaritan woman <note>A reference to the woman at the well in John 4:1-42, who asks Jesus for "living water."</note> asked for grace
troubled me, and the haste pricked me
along the obstructed way behind my leader,
and I grieved for the just vengeance <note>The punishment of the souls on the terrace of Avarice.</note>.
And behold, just as Luke describes to us:
that Christ appeared to two who along the way
had already gone out from the sepulchral tomb,
a shade appeared to us, and it came behind us,
looking from its feet at the crowd that lies there;
nor were we aware of it until it spoke first,
saying: "My brothers, may God give you peace."
We turned suddenly, and Virgil
returned to him the sign that is appropriate for that.

<column-break/>

**THE NATURAL THIRST.** He shows us that there can be an innate thirst and desire in man to know. And because the knowledge of divine things is that through which we are blessed, we cannot have this perfectly through our own industry nor by natural ways unless we are illuminated by the Holy Spirit. Which Christ indicated in the Gospel of Saint John, Chapter IV, when asking for a drink from the Samaritan woman at the well of Jacob; and she denying it to him, alleging that the Jews do not associate with Samaritans. He added: "if you knew who it is who asks you for a drink, you would have asked him, and he would have given you to drink from a water of a fountain that springs up into eternal life." <note>original: "fons aquae salientis in vitam aeternam"</note> The young woman, then, after many words, asked for the grace, and Christ filled her with the Holy Spirit. Therefore, most wisely, the poet shows at present that the natural thirst—that is, the natural desire for knowing and understanding—is never satisfied except with the water. Wherefore the young Samaritan woman asked for grace—that is, the grace of the Holy Spirit. **IT TROUBLED ME.** <note>original: "mitravagliava"</note> This is a metaphor <term>translation: a figurative use of a word</term> from grain already threshed, which, so that it remains purged and clean, is "travailed"—that is, they make it pass from sieve to sieve <note>The commentator connects the word "travailed" (troubled) with "vagliare" (to sieve or winnow), suggesting a process of refinement.</note>; thus our soul, wishing to find the truth, goes on purging itself from time to time. **AND THE HASTE PRICKED ME** shows that at the same time the soul was eager to investigate the cause of the shaking of the mountain and the song of the souls, and the body had to hurry in following its journey. But Statius, arriving, explains that which neither Dante—that is, sensuality—nor Virgil—that is, human intellect, although illuminated by much learning—could understand by themselves. But Statius, who because of being accustomed to such things, explains them. And he puts Statius for the human intellect, which extends to comprehending that which cannot be understood by way of reason. And by comparison he shows, according to what Luke writes in the twenty-third chapter <note>The commentator likely means Luke 24, which describes Christ appearing to two disciples on the road to Emmaus.</note>.

<summary>This page introduces Canto XXI, where Dante and Virgil meet the spirit of the poet Statius, who is likened to the resurrected Christ appearing to disciples. The accompanying commentary explores the human "natural thirst" for divine knowledge, using the biblical figure of the Samaritan woman as an allegory for the soul's need for the Holy Spirit.</summary>
<keywords>Statius, natural thirst, Samaritan woman, Holy Spirit, divine knowledge, Virgil, Luke the Evangelist, winnowing metaphor</keywords>

<meta>Following the previous study on fluid dynamics and the balance of water levels in connected vessels, this page shifts focus toward solid mechanics. Leonardo continues his investigation into equilibrium, now exploring how three suspended weights interact when moved along curved or intersecting geometric paths relative to a central point of gravity.</meta>

<note>A pen and ink geometric diagram by Leonardo da Vinci exploring the balance of three weights, labeled n, m, and q, relative to a central point and curved paths. The drawing uses a complex system of arcs and vertical alignments to hypothesize mechanical equilibrium. The structure includes vertical lines and intersecting arcs, with the weights depicted as squares hanging from a baseline.</note>

If you pull the three <term>heavy bodies</term> <note>original: "gravi"; physical weights or masses subject to the force of gravity.</note> at equal distances from the <term>center of the world</term> <note>original: "ciētro del modo"; a Renaissance term for the center of gravity, which was believed to be at the center of the Earth.</note>, they will come to be caught [at] n. They make those which [are at] o and q come to points m and d, in a <term>lenticular</term> <note>original: "lēticolā"; shaped like a lens or a double curve.</note> way. Regarding points n, m, and q: if you could make points n, m, and q [reach] p, s, d, and q, then from n, m, and q would come point o, d, q, b, s, d, and q. And points n, m, and q, having come to points b, s, d, and q, will be able to make points n, m, and q come into point d. And points n, m, and q will come to make s and s. length; one must do so because one has about 20 fathoms of water there; subsequently, one must stay on the same side about a cable's length from that island, where one then encounters shallower water, namely 8, 7, and 6 fathoms, and where it is narrowest, 5 fathoms, which depth one keeps until one reaches the roadstead. Thus, with God's help, one can enter there, provided one keeps close to the mentioned island; on the starboard side, as one enters the strait, it is somewhat shallow, but that reveals itself clearly. There are 2 small islands, one is called <margin>The islands Puloway and Pulorin.</margin> Puloway, the other Pulorin, which lie about 3 miles westward as one enters the strait; one is in no danger from them, as one easily becomes aware of them; one can leave them, whether one is entering or exiting, on either side as one wishes.

Around the middle of March, we found <margin>Steady winds of 4, 5, 3 months.</margin> the wind quite variable here, which remained so until the middle of April, from which time it remains, to our best knowledge, between east and southeast for 4 months: but the inhabitants there told us that it usually remains that way for 5 months, just as it is between west and northwest for 5 months thereafter, and the 2 remaining months are variable. Here, by the dark of the moon, there is much misty and rainy weather. We stayed at Banda for 21 weeks and 6 days, during which time we had 11 deaths, mostly from the <term>loop</term> <gloss>dysentery/flux</gloss>.

On the 21st of July, Sunday, we set sail from Banda with an east-southeasterly wind and set our course westward. On the 22nd, <margin>Burro.</margin> we reached the southern side of Burro <note>modern-day Buru, Indonesia</note>; the wind as above. On the 27th, at the height of Deselem, <margin>Deselem.</margin> near the south end of the island, leaving 7 islands on the port side. We held our course northward, close to the main island of Deselem, to keep ourselves clear of a small island and a sandbank that...

<margin>Celebes.</margin>
at the southwest of Deselem lies; subsequently deviating from this island, we set our course north-northwest along the western side of Deselem and reached 6 degrees 10 minutes, and sailed 18 miles westward; thus we came near the bank that lies at the southwest end of Celebes <note>modern-day Sulawesi</note>, the outermost corner of which lies to the west of the bank at 6 degrees; having passed this, we proceeded further westward.

<margin>Arrive back before Bantam.</margin>
On the 16th of August, we again came to anchor at the roadstead of Bantam.

<margin>And depart from there for home.</margin>
On the 6th of October, we set sail from here with the *Draak* and the *Ascension*.

<margin>A sunken island.</margin>
On the 15th of November, we were at a latitude of 31 degrees 48 minutes, having the wind north-northwest, with thick and misty weather. On that same day, around 10 o'clock in the morning, we arrived within a ship's length of a reef or sunken island, where the water was brownish and muddy, and in some places bluish; when we were a ship's width or 2 away from it, we saw the water to the side of the ship as black and thick as if it were earth or coarse sand being thrown up from it. The variation here is 21 degrees, decreasing from the north to the west.

<margin>The Land of Ethiopia.</margin>
On the 16th of December, we had 9 miles west, and the latitude of 34 degrees 20 minutes. At that time, we saw the land of Ethiopia <note>a historical term often referring to the African coast near the Cape</note>, by estimation 12 miles or thereabouts away from us. On the 26th, we...

<margin>Cape of Good Hope.</margin>
were at 34 degrees 30 minutes, and thus at the latitude and in sight of the Cape of Good Hope, not even a mile from it; therefore we took our course north-northwest and north, according to how the land lies around the Cape.

<margin>Saldania.</margin>
On the 27th, we came to anchor at the roadstead of Saldania, where we found the *Draak*, our Admiral, and the *Hector*; the former had arrived there 7 days earlier, after having been tossed back and forth about 4 miles from the Cape of Good Hope, having no more than 10 men left on board; all his other crew had passed away, numbering 53 who had died since their departure from Bantam, and that in the span of 9 months. The *Susanna* had become separated from them 3 months after they had departed from Bantam, and nothing had been heard of her since. Here we came to anchor in 7 fathoms of water, having the low point to the northwest by west, and the Sugar Loaf <note>a descriptive name for a mountain, likely Lion's Head</note> south-southwest and half a point toward the west; the point of Penguin Island <note>original: "Pengwins Eyland"</note> northwest by north, the mountain between the Sugar Loaf and the lower or low point, west-southwest.

# LOPO SOARES d'ALBEGERIA.

<margin>1516.</margin>
A certain man, who made some signs to the ships, was ordered by Lopo to be approached by Bastiaan Rodrigues with a boat to see what this person desired. He was a renegade who spoke very good Spanish, and he brought a 
<margin>Challenge letter from Suleiman to Lopo Soares.</margin>
Challenge Letter from Suleiman to Lopo Soares, which was full of the usual Turkish boasting and broad claims, challenging him to a battle at sea or on land, one against one, or many against many, to prevent the shedding of the blood of entire armies. And notwithstanding that Gaspar da Silva and Don Alfonso de Menezes begged Lopo Soares very heartily to grant them that honor, he said to the Moor that he should go and tell Suleiman: 
<margin>Answer thereto.</margin>
That he hoped to bring the answer to him on land himself. The next day, as if in satisfaction of their request, Lopo Soares ordered Don Alfonso de Menezes and Denis Fernandes de Mello to go and sound the bottom of the entire channel with a galley; and while they were busy with that, other captains 
<margin>Arson in the Moorish ships.</margin>
went with some boats to set fire to some ships that were lying in the middle of the channel. This being done, he also made himself master of a galleon and immediately set it in a full flame, so that those in the city thought that the fire would spread to them, whereby they began to make every preparation 
<margin>Fear of the inhabitants.</margin>
to flee from there. Seeing all this turmoil, Suleiman began to say: Gentlemen and 
<margin>Suleiman's address to the people.</margin>
Friends, where do you wish to go? What are you afraid of? Do you not see that these people have been here for three days already and have burned nothing but this galleon, which they found defenseless? If you think that they will come to land, you are deceived, for if anyone wants to go to land, he will not burn a galleon, but rather head straight for it and take it; therefore, return to your houses, for this is not the people who would want to risk themselves in such danger.

to set fire to; and so that we may strike as much terror into them from here as the bolts do over there, let us show them a trial outside the walls, that we are not as unprepared for everything here as they believe. Finally, with such and similar 
<margin>The effect thereof.</margin>
exhortations, he brought the people back to a standstill and into good order, with a great display of their flags and standards, and much violence along the River, going out of one gate and back into another: and above the walls, where 
<margin>Misdeeds of the inhabitants following that.</margin>
all the people were piled upon one another, the shouting was so terrifying that, notwithstanding that our men lay a mile from there, it still rang in their ears to the point of annoyance. They also fired from time to time from three or four pieces that were well thirty palms long, with cannonballs as large as a man's head, some of which went skipping between the ships, but it pleased God that none of them caused any particular damage.

Lopo Soares, meanwhile, having understood from Don Alfonso and Denis Fernandes that one could not enter the channel except with much turning and winding, and that notwithstanding that the rowing ships were light, they nevertheless ran great danger because the Moors had positioned their artillery in such a way that it could cause much damage to our men, he decided secretly with some captains, and two or three Christians, 
<margin>Decision of Lopo Soares thereon.</margin>
those who had escaped from the vessel, that they should go and spike that artillery at night with a sloop, who would be followed by others who would meanwhile set fire to the galleys lying in the inner harbor. But none of these things came to fruition, because the prisoners, after this had been held up to them with the promise of great rewards if it succeeded, 
<margin>Their answer.</margin>
gave for answer that it was exposing themselves to certain death, without any fruit, because at night one kept watch over the pieces and the galleys, but that it seemed better to them to crawl upon the city, and that whenever the Moors saw such, they might perhaps abandon it, as they seemed to want to do at the mere sight of his fleet out of fear.

<meta>This page continues the technical discussion of monastic discipline (Vinaya), specifically focusing on the rules governing the Kaṭhina period—a time after the summer retreat when monks are granted special privileges regarding their robes.</meta>

# Pelliot chinois 3113

Regarding the equipment for luxury robes and the rules for **not losing the privilege of the robe** <note>During the Kaṭhina period, monks are permitted to be separated from their three robes without committing an offense. "Losing the robe" refers to the expiration of this special privilege.</note>. In the midst of water, if a few people draw water, even at night; or as some say, within the constant flow of a river, one must not stop or bury [the boundary]. 

The markers for the boundary are determined by eight trees, seven intervals, and sixty-two steps. These serve to partition the surface. If we discuss the **Pavāraṇā sheds** <note>Pavāraṇā (self-correction) is the ceremony held at the end of the rainy season retreat; "sheds" refers to the temporary structures or designated areas for this rite.</note>, there are fifteen types:

1.  Where the Sangha is absent, and the two times are not listed.
2.  Fruit trees, where the trees are interconnected; it is permitted for someone to guard them, and the interior is restricted by a screen.
3.  Where gaps are established by ten fingers' width <note>A traditional unit of measurement in the Vinaya.</note>, specifically screened; if in a place with fruit, it must be treated four times over.
4.  Where the establishment is constant.
5.  Where the middle is not yet reached.
6.  Where practitioners walk a great distance and return; the interior is double-screened. 
7.  If the area is insufficient, six types of boundaries are listed; the boundary is for the time of return and the location.
8.  A wooden boundary; "middle" refers to the markers of the fields where one stays.
9.  A screened boundary; after the screening, the time is fixed to the location.
10. A room boundary; a place where many scattered repairs are made.
11. A house boundary; where numbers are stored in six locations.
12. **An island boundary**; involving lakes or rivers; if one studies there, even if the time passes, one does not lose the robe privilege.
13. **A well boundary**; involving secret paths and irrigation; if one stays overnight and places their robe there, they do not lose the privilege during their stay.
14. [Missing in original sequence]
15. A boundary where there are many people, or a small sea, or the sands and stones of the south. <gloss>Bulrushes</gloss> A path through the surging waves. These two boundaries are established by name.

There are two types of "reaches" <note>likely referring to coastal or river reaches</note> at the boundary's edge. When people of three types arrive, seeking a common residence, they establish the **Kaushambi** <note>original: 憍薩彌 (Qiāosàmí). This likely refers to a legal precedent or specific tradition regarding the Kaṭhina robe from the city of Kosambi.</note> foundation. If there are people within the boundary together with the monastery, or if they are outside the boundary, or if they are not in order, the boundary may be large or slightly different. If they merge into one later, it follows the Kaushambi extension.

If within a large boundary there is a monastery, and the outside of the boundary is not confused and does not flow together, then later scriptures mention villages like Tangmai and Yicun. 

According to the **Vinaya** <term>Vinaya: The code of monastic discipline.</term>, if there is no established Law <note>Dharma-rule</note>, and one is within a village, the robe is protected. Because this matter is not yet according to the Law, the "Path" is considered the Law. It does not matter if there is a village or not; the Law of the Vinaya flows through. If a village existed first, one follows the Law and later establishes the unified "Golden Cloister." 

If an outsider has not yet entered, the rule states that the head of the teaching is not within the boundary. If one departs from the village, a new boundary path is made. If there is a village marker, and the village acts improperly, it is called an "Empty Kaṭhina." According to the meaning, one seeks the Kaṭhina through the village marker. If it is not a Kaṭhina, the robes are not yet relinquished. 

If a person enters and the robe is not under the Kaṭhina boundary, and they stay within the riverbed, the robes accumulate merit to the limits of the village. If the village is gone, or if the markers of the teaching are not established, it is not a robe boundary. This is fixed. Therefore, next we remove the robes and the deep Kaṭhina teachings. This is the ultimate discussion.

**Question:** When there is a village, can one borrow it first? How is the Kaṭhina removed?
**Answer:** According to the Vinaya, it does not matter if it exists or not. One first observes the surroundings, then relinquishes the robe. If the relinquishing of the robe follows the Law, one can first establish the Kaṭhina markers. If one speaks of the method of removal, and says it follows the previous village markers, the current Law is not the Kaṭhina. 

Regarding the **Taking of the Kaṭhina**: The Vinaya says if a village existed previously, first observe the surroundings and rely on the previous clothing. If one takes the Kaṭhina outside the boundary, that is the "True Kaṭhina." Because it is a new Law, it is called the "Path Kaṭhina Boundary." If it is doubled, it is a new name and does not depend on the boundary. Among those who follow the Law, the witnesses manage the matter. In harmony, they follow the Law to modify and fix the robes. If the various parts of the body are too short or mismatched, it is decided by the Law.

Between the Kaṭhina and the village boundaries: one follows the markers of the village. The village boundary is the Kaṭhina boundary. Furthermore, when many people divide the merit, they obtain the boundary. Regarding the village, if one enters the village against the flow: 
According to the Vinaya, at the very beginning, there is a gap of one Kaṭhina. The "Faithful Kaṭhina" robe follows the Law. Furthermore, if one acts as a boundary companion, and the place fully has the Kaṭhina, the boundary is within the path. 

**Question:** Regarding staying overnight with the Kaṭhina robe? 
**Answer:** One follows the Law. If there is a gap, one follows the Law. Whether it is Kaṭhina or not, if it is by a river or stream, and the boundary is scattered or the boundaries of the "Color Limit" are fallen, and people do not know the markers: if there are houses in the middle, the robe rule says one must know the method of steps. Whether it is Kaṭhina or not is determined by the "Kaṭhina of Faith." One follows the twelve steps and relies on the gap. If this single gap of the robe is not a village, the markers are few. One can name it the "Kaṭhina of Faith." If the houses are not mismatched, they share the same nature.

There are three types of "Staff Paths": 
1. Utilizing the robe boundary and releasing many.
4. The village path in two places, with Kaṭhina markers appearing to be exhausted.

One checks the numbers and followers, then later determines the **Natural Kaṭhina of Faith**. Those who are not following the Law refuse the boundary and the restricted path of the Kaṭhina. Using the name of the path to differentiate a single interval, the Kaṭhina boundary does not follow the Law. Because of this, within the Kaṭhina boundary, there is a Natural Kaṭhina boundary. 

The signs do not necessarily need to be six or seven. For instance, in a village, most are village boundaries. If they are fixed and established and do not rely on each other, or if they are divided according to the Law, then the markers are for the Buddha's Law. The Kaṭhina signs rely on themselves. Afterwards, one marker, once it receives the Kaṭhina, if it rises to refuse the Law, it is the Kaṭhina marker. 

Within the curves, one follows the "Bucket Kaṭhina Boundary" and trusts it. Secondly, following the Law, one trusts the Kaṭhina boundary. Because of this boundary Law, within the two, a natural faith arises. The power of the two boundaries is divided; each boundary naturally has a Kaṭhina robe boundary. Because the exterior place does not follow the Law's modification, there is power.

If it is not according to the Law, it is the "Correct Kaṭhina." This "Surging Shape" below creates the Kaṭhina robe markers. Below it creates the Law Kaṭhina, which is also a flowing robe. The judgment of the flow is exhausted by the teaching robe's minimal division. Facing the "Correct Kaṭhina," the Vinaya calls it the "Fixed Kaṭhina." Following the Law provides the strength of the Kaṭhina robe. 

The **Natural Kaṭhina Robe** has "Bridge Stones" upon which the strength is divided. There is an explanation of the markers, as there were errors previously. 
**Question:** Regarding the strength of the Natural Kaṭhina land? 
**Answer:** The robe can be separated like a breast-child <note>Meaning it can be legally separated from the monk's person</note>. If one seeks the division of strength, it is the restricted Law outside the village markers. If that village is not a village, the land outside the markers where the strength is divided is where the "Heart-Governing Stone" is located. The **Kaṭhina Stone Boundary** is a type of stone boundary. 

1. A Natural Kaṭhina that does not disappear. The Vinaya recites that one side has a "Face-Washing Marker." Half of the text says the "Initial Hair Screen." This is also it.
2. Kaṭhina Ponds, etc. Looking at the Kaṭhina's construction, they are shown together. The Kaṭhina exists only within the Kaṭhina; it is not outside. It is also named "Not-Nine." 
3. Regarding the markers, the robes must not be mismatched first. When the Kaṭhina is released, the Bhikkhu <note>monk</note> follows his inclination. When the Kaṭhina is descending, the robes are not... <unclear>loss of text</unclear>

<summary>This page details the complex legalities of the Kaṭhina period, listing fifteen types of boundaries (sima) where monks can maintain their robe privileges and discussing how village boundaries interact with monastic law.</summary>
<keywords>Kaṭhina, Sima, Vinaya, Robe Privileges, Pavāraṇā, Monastic Boundaries, Kosambi, Natural Boundaries, Buddhist Law</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the specific interpretations of solar phenomena from Volume 139 of the Wubizhi. Following the previous page’s focus on "Back-arcs" and their relation to military rebellion, this section defines "Jasper Rings" and "Straight Pillars," detailing how their number and orientation predict the success of uprisings and the division of territory.</meta>

# Treatise on Armament Technology, Volume 139
## Divination of the Sun (Part II)

### Page 8

The **Jasper Ring** <term>original: *Qiong* (璚); a sash-like atmospheric arc or ring-like phenomenon</term> is shaped like a sash. If **Jasper Rings** appear on all four sides of the sun, or if five colors shimmer and sparkle beside the sun on a single day, this is defined as a **Jasper Ring**.

This omen signifies that the state will have joyful celebrations, yet the wilderness will suffer from wind and rain. When two armies face one another, the side where this phenomenon is positioned will suffer defeat. On a single day, it may also signify the presence of a rebel, or that a minister is plotting treason, leading to the deaths of ten thousand people beneath him. If four or five **Jasper Rings** appear, the number of rebels will correspond to the number of rings observed.

When blue and red vapors are long and stand vertically beside the sun, this is called a **Straight Pillar** <term>original: *Zhi* (直); likely referring to parhelia or sun pillars</term>. Alternatively, if mixed vapors resemble the character for "river" <note>original: *chuan* (川); a character composed of three vertical lines</note> leaning against the sun, this is also a **Straight Pillar**. This portends military chaos and the fragmentation of the national territory.

If there is one **Straight Pillar** beside the sun, it indicates an enemy on that side who desires to declare independence. If there are **Straight Pillars** on all four sides, it indicates that in all four directions there are those who wish to declare themselves independent rulers. The side that launches an attack from the direction where the pillar is located will be victorious.

If there are three **Straight Pillars** and three **Embraces** <term>original: *Bao* (抱); tangent arcs that curve toward the sun, usually seen as a protective or favorable sign</term> beside the sun, those who wish to declare independence will not succeed. The side that follows the direction of the **Embrace** will be victorious and will kill the enemy general.

<summary>This page explains the divinatory meaning of "Jasper Rings" and "Straight Pillars," interpreting these solar phenomena as omens of ministerial treason, territorial fragmentation, and the outcome of regional attempts at independence.</summary>
<keywords>Jasper Ring, Straight Pillar, solar divination, parhelia, military omens, rebellion, independence, Embrace arc</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of "Straight Pillars" (Zhi) from the previous page, specifically detailing how their colors and clarity determine the outcome of a minister's rebellion. It then transitions into "Intersections" (Jiao) and "Solar Mouths" (Kou), relating these atmospheric shapes to military victory, internal discord, and the political ambitions of regional lords.</meta>

# Treatise on Armament Technology, Volume 139
## Divination of the Sun (Part II)

### Page 9

...ent.

If the sun has **Yellow Straight Pillars** <term>original: *Zhi* (直); vertical atmospheric phenomena resembling pillars of light</term>, it indicates that the ruler is properly establishing his ministers. However, if the **Straight Pillars** appear blue or red, it signifies that ministers are attempting to establish themselves as independent rulers.

If a **Straight Pillar** is red in the center and blue on the outside, those seeking to declare independence will not succeed. However, if the phenomenon appears yellow or white and looks moist and lustrous, their bid for power will be successful.

When blue and red vapors take the shape of two straight lines intersecting—whether positioned above, below, to the left, or to the right of the sun—this is called an **Intersection** <term>original: *Jiao* (交)</term>. Such **Intersections** are omens of **Excess** <term>original: *Yin* (淫); referring to licentiousness, social imbalance, or transgressive behavior</term>.

This vapor primarily governs the presence of licentious actions. If intersecting red clouds appear beside the sun, there will be military conflict <note>literally "there are soldiers/weapons"</note> in the lands below.

If two vapors on either side of the sun intersect, pierce through one another, or face away from each other, it signifies that great armies will rise across the world. It also portends internal rebellion and discord within the military. Another interpretation states: if there is an **Intersection** beside the sun, the army that attacks from the direction of that intersection will emerge victorious.

When various vapors form the shape of the character for "mouth" <note>original: *kou* (口); a simple square shape in Chinese script</note> near the edge of the sun, it is called a **Solar Mouth**. The appearance of one or two such "mouths" indicates that treacherous and evil people are causing harm. If three, four, or five **Solar Mouths** appear, it signifies that princes and marquises are plotting to seize power and establish themselves as independent sovereigns.

<summary>This section details how vertical pillars and intersecting vapors around the sun predict the success of ministerial rebellions and the movement of great armies. It also introduces "Solar Mouths" as omens of political conspiracy by high-ranking lords.</summary>
<keywords>Straight Pillars (Zhi), Intersections (Jiao), Solar Mouth (Kou), rebellion, military victory, treacherous ministers, Wubizhi</keywords>

Therefore, by being careful with the scales and the plumb line, and by being accurate in judging weights, one is sufficient to govern within the borders. <gloss>Scales and balances represent equality. The plumb line represents straightness and law.</gloss> Thus, one who embodies the Great One is clear about the essence of Heaven and Earth and understands the order of Virtue and the Way. Their hearing and sight shine like the sun and moon. Their spirit communicates with the myriad things. Their movement and stillness are attuned to Yin and Yang. Their joy and anger are harmonized with the Four Seasons. Their virtuous bounty is applied beyond the borders, and their fame is passed to later generations. One who models themselves on Yin and Yang has virtue that joins with Heaven and Earth. Their brilliance equals the sun and moon. Their essence is united with the ghosts and spirits. They wear the roundness of Heaven and walk upon the squareness of Earth. They hold the standard and embrace the plumb line. <gloss>Round represents Heaven, square represents Earth. The standard is for correction, and the line is for straightness.</gloss> Internally, they can govern their own bodies. Externally, they can win over the people. <gloss>Winning over the people means gaining their joyful hearts.</gloss> When they issue orders, everyone in the world follows them like the wind. Those who follow the Four Seasons are soft but not brittle, firm but not easily broken. <gloss>Broken refers to snapping.</gloss> They are broad but not loose. <gloss>Loose refers to being too slow or lax.</gloss> They are solemn but not contrary. <gloss>Solemn refers to being urgent or strict.</gloss>

They are gentle and compliant in order to nurture the various species. <gloss>Species refers to all living things.</gloss> Their virtue encompasses the foolish and tolerates the unworthy, having no selfish love. <gloss>Selfishness refers to being crooked or partial.</gloss> One who uses the Six Pitch-pipes punishes chaos and prohibits violence. They promote the worthy and discard the unworthy. They support and adjust things to make them correct. <gloss>Supporting and adjusting refers to taking charge and governing.</gloss> They break down dangers to make things level and correct what is crooked to make it straight. <gloss>Correcting what is crooked means straightening the bent.</gloss> They are clear about the way of forbidding and permitting, of opening and closing. They ride upon the times and follow the momentum to employ the hearts of men. <gloss>Employ refers to making use of.</gloss> If an Emperor only models himself on Yin and Yang, he will be encroached upon. <gloss>Encroached upon means being invaded by the various states of the Central Plains.</gloss> If a King only follows the Four Seasons, he will be diminished. <gloss>Diminished refers to having territory taken by others.</gloss> If a Hegemon only regulates with the Six Pitch-pipes, he will be insulted. <gloss>Insulted means being mocked by neighboring states.</gloss> If a Ruler loses the standard and the plumb line, he will be deposed. <gloss>Deposed means being removed by his ministers and replaced with a worthy ruler.</gloss> Therefore, if one who is small tries to act on a large scale, he will be inconsistent and lose the closeness of others. <gloss>Inconsistent means not being full or dense. Losing closeness means not having the loyalty of his ministers.</gloss> If one who is great acts on a small scale, he will be narrow and unable to contain others. <gloss>Acting on a small scale makes the government narrow and unable to encompass the ministers.</gloss> When the noble and the lowly do not lose their proper form, the world is governed.

A <term>tong</term> is 100 <term>li</term> square. Within the <term>tong</term> are four <term>du</term>, each 80 <term>li</term> square, which produce land taxes. Along the edges, a 10 <term>li</term> strip is used to manage the <term>hui</term>. Four <term>dian</term> <gloss>administrative units of 400 wells</gloss> make a <term>xian</term> <gloss>district</gloss>. Four [such units] ascend to a <term>tong</term>. The <term>tong</term> is 80 <term>li</term> square, and by adding 10 <term>li</term> to the sides, it becomes 100 <term>li</term> square. Calculating the 80 <term>li</term> of the <term>tong</term> by squaring it gives 6,400 wells and 57,600 husbandmen producing taxes. ...the group of sixteen modifications, their objects, and the entire expansion of the universe shines as the <term>Śrī Cakra</term>. ||108||

He describes the worship of the <term>Śrī Cakra</term> beginning with "Gaṇeśa" and ending with "having performed the circle worship" (3.168)—

"One should worship Gaṇeśa and Dūtarī, as well as Kṣetreśa and Dūtikā,
At the external gate, O Goddess, and also the goddesses such as Svastikā." ||109||

One should worship Gaṇeśa at the doorframe of the <term>Śrī Cakra</term>, his power Dūtarī, Kṣetreśa known as Baṭuka, and his power Dūtikā. It is said in the *Saṅketa-paddhati*:

"He who is capable of dispelling the darkness of the night of great delusion, which is duality and non-duality,
The unique Gaṇeśa, along with Dūtarī, shines like the sun.
Where the supreme expansion of intuition occurs, another like the moon,
Baṭuka, who is full of the dance, shines along with Dūtī."

At the external gate, in the region outside the door of the <term>Śrī Cakra</term>, one should worship the goddesses such as Svastikā—namely, Sarasvatī, Śrī, Durgā, and Bhadrakālī, these four. The term "Svastikā, etc." is a compound <note>meaning Svastikā is the first of these</note>. Svāhā, Śubhaṅkarī, Gaurī, Lokadhātrī, and Vāgīśvarī—these are the five. The practitioner should worship these goddesses. This is famous in the ritual manuals. ||109||

<summary>The text provides specific instructions for the ritual worship of deities at the gates of the Sri Chakra, framing them as aspects of consciousness that clear away dualistic ignorance.</summary>

...these goddesses. This is famous in the ritual manuals. ||109||

"Then, inside the triangle also, one should worship the lineage of Gurus, which resides in three ways."

Then, inside the triangle of that <term>Śrī Cakra</term>, one should worship the lineage of Gurus—the sequence of Gurus starting from Shiva up to one's own Guru—which resides in three parts: the <term>divyaugha</term> <gloss>divine lineage</gloss>, <term>siddhaugha</term> <gloss>lineage of perfected beings</gloss>, and <term>mānavaugha</term> <gloss>lineage of humans</gloss>. The word "also" implies "one should worship." The lineage of Gurus must be learned only from the mouth of the Guru, not from people in general. Nor is it written in a book, due to it being extremely secret.

"Inside that, having invoked the Great Goddess, one should worship her again. ||110||
She who resides in the center of the Great Lotus Forest, whose body is the Bliss of the Cause,
The Goddess who resides on my lap, the bestower of the fruit of all desired intentions." ||111||

Inside that, in the center of the <term>Śrī Cakra</term>, in the circle called the <term>Baindava</term> <gloss>the center point</gloss>. She who resides in the center of the Great Lotus Forest, as described in "the Guru's sandals in the *Vāgbhava* <gloss>seat of speech</gloss> residing in the center of the Great Lotus Forest" (3.15).

<meta>This page continues the ritual sequence from the previous page. Having concluded the rites for Mercury (Budha), the text now focuses on Jupiter (Bṛhaspati/Guru). The structure includes the meditation (dhyānam) which provides a visual description of the deity for the practitioner, followed by several celebratory verses (stotram), and concluding with the Shadanga-nyāsa, where the power of the mantras is "installed" into the practitioner's heart, head, hair, torso, eyes, and hands to prepare them for the main ceremony.</meta>

...twice, facing all directions. These are to be known as the **Gurus** <note>original: "Guru," another name for Jupiter, meaning "Teacher" or "Heavy with knowledge"</note>; thus they are proclaimed.

### Now, the Meditation

Adorned with gems like those of Indra, the Lord of the World, who is the life of all that lives. The Lord of Speech <note>original: "Vākpati"</note>, whose intellect and beauty are vast, who is Prosperity herself. With a crown that holds the entire universe of beings, he whose lotus feet are seen at the limit of vision. With a pure mind and marvelous intent, for the sake of all auspiciousness, may the Lord of Speech be well-pleased with those of unwavering heart. ॥ 1 ॥

There is none equal in pervasiveness; he is the Priest of the Gods. The knower of all deities, the Teacher—salutations, salutations to him. ॥ 3 ॥

The Teacher of the gods, wearing yellow garments, the Lord of the Sages. I bow to him who lives as the most excellent of the moving stars. ॥ 4 ॥

The Teacher of the gods and the seers, shining like gold, the relative of the three worlds, the peaceful one—I bow to Jupiter. ॥ 5 ॥

The proclaimer of all scriptures, the expander of all actions, the giver of all success, the god who is affectionate toward his circle of devotees. ॥ 6 ॥ <margin>6</margin>

---

The giver of boons, the peaceful one, worshiped by the thirty gods <note>a traditional grouping of the Vedic pantheon</note>, the supreme. For him whose seat is the sacred grass and who is of golden hue, this offering is made. ॥ 7 ॥

Clad in yellow garments, the holy one, endowed with the splendor of the sun.

**Thus ends the Ritual Assignment for the Teacher.**

*Om*, [earth, atmosphere, heavens], salutations to the **thumbs**.
"One [form] of yours is bright, the other is fit for sacrifice..." <note>original: "śukraṃ te anyad yajataṃ te anyad," a verse from Rig Veda 6.58.1 usually associated with the sun or brightness, here used for the ritual installation</note>
"...like the two-fold paths of the sun." To the **middle fingers**, salutations.
"You protect all magic, O self-dependent power." To the **ring fingers**, salutations.
"May your auspicious gift be near to us." To the **ring fingers**, salutations. <note>The text repeats the ring finger assignment, likely a scribal duplication or indicating a specific rhythmic touch</note>
Having uttered the entire mantra, to the **palms and backs of the hands**.

### Now begins the Six-Limbed Ritual Assignment

*Om*, [earth, atmosphere, heavens], salutations to the **heart**.
"One [form] of yours is bright, the other is fit for sacrifice"—*Svāhā* <note>a ritual exclamation used when offering into fire</note> to the **head**.
"The day and night of various forms"—*Vaṣaṭ* <note>a ritual exclamation for empowerment</note> to the **topknot**.
"You protect all magic, O self-dependent power"—*Huṃ* <note>a protective, seed-syllable sound</note> to the **armor** <note>the torso/shoulders</note>.
"May your auspicious gift be near to us"—*Vauṣaṭ* to the **three eyes**.
Having uttered the entire mantra—*Phaṭ* <note>a sharp sound used to dispel obstacles</note> to the **weapon** <note>symbolized by snapping fingers or clapping</note>.

### Now, the Ritual Assignment of the Feet

*Om*...

<meta>This page continues the ritual cycle of the Nine Planets (Navagraha). Having concluded the rites for Jupiter on the previous page, the manuscript now moves to the ritual installation (nyāsa) and meditation (dhyānam) for Venus (Shukra) and begins the sequence for Saturn (Shani). The practitioner is instructed to mentally or physically "place" the divine energy of these celestial bodies onto specific parts of their own body.</meta>

<page-num>7</page-num>

<margin>Na</margin> <note>Likely a folio marker or shorthand</note> Earth, Atmosphere, Heaven <note>original: "Bhūr-bhuvaḥ svaḥ"</note> — the hair-lock. Venus <note>original: "Shukra"</note> in my head. Then at the seat... My hymns in the sacrifice... in the eyes. In the nostrils... *Vashat!* <note>a ritual exclamation used when making an offering</note>. Like the sky on the arms... on the two ankles... on the heart... on the belly. On the joints... in the speech... in the pair of thighs... on the knees. Thus... on the feet. **Now, the ritual installation in the hands. Thus, the ritual installation in the feet.**

Om. The seer of this mantra for Venus is Bharadvāja, placed in the mouth; the meter is Trishṭup, placed in the heart.

### Now, the Meditation on the Arts

The all-knowing giver of subjects, the shaker of the gods. Subtle... like a goddess <note>original: "Shākinī," a class of female spirits or yoginis</note>. ॥ 1 ॥

The one art of Venus... known as the form of the head... teacher... of all the gods... may he destroy the sins through serpent-wisdom <note>original: "Nāgaviyo"</note>. ॥ 2 ॥ <margin>7</margin>

---

...through success, of balanced mind, having obtained special knowledge. The leader and guide of the sons of the demons <note>original: "Daityas"</note>. The one who calms the serpent-wisdom, the peaceful one. ॥ 3 ॥

<insert>Shukra</insert> <note>Added by a later scribe to clarify the subject</note>
The syllable "A," the supreme teacher of the demons. I bow to the one in the lineage of the serpents, the proclaimer of all scriptures. ॥ 4 ॥

### Thus ends the ritual installation of Venus. Now, the ritual installation of Saturn.

Om. Earth, Atmosphere, Heaven. **Salutations to the two thumbs.**
"May the fire be peaceful with its fires" — **to the two index fingers.**
"May the Sun burn peacefully for us" — **to the two middle fingers.**
"May the wind..." — **to the two ring fingers.**
"May the waters..." — **to the two little fingers.**
Reciting the entire mantra — **to the palms and the backs of the hands.**

### Now, the installation in the six limbs

Om. Earth, Atmosphere, Heaven — **Salutations to the heart.**
"May the fire be peaceful with its fires" — **Swāhā <note>an invocation used when offering to fire</note> to the head.**
"May the Sun burn peacefully for us" — **Vaṣat to the hair-lock.**
"The gift of rays..." — **Hum <note>a protective seed-syllable</note> to the armor.** <note>refers to the chest and torso</note>
"May the waters..." — **Vauṣat to the three eyes.**
Reciting the entire mantra — **Phat <note>a mantra used to dispel obstacles</note> to the "weapon" ritual gesture.**

### Now, the ritual installation in the feet

Om. Earth, Atmosphere...

The text transitions into the specific finger and limb gestures required for Saturn's propitiation.</summary>

## Leaf 1 (Top)

As <term>Vidya Lakshmi</term> <gloss>the Goddess of Knowledge and Prosperity</gloss> is seen, so also is <term>Saraswati</term> <gloss>the Goddess of Wisdom and Arts</gloss> seen. She is the giver of all knowledge and the provider of all wealth.
<note>original: "Vidyalakshmi yatha drishta tatha drishta Saraswati | Sarva vidya pradatree cha sarva sampath pradayinee ||"</note>

To the most auspicious of all auspicious things, to the one who brings success to all goals, to the protector, the three-eyed one, the golden goddess, to <term>Narayani</term> <gloss>the feminine aspect of the Supreme Lord</gloss>, I bow to you.
<note>original: "Sarva mangala mangalye Shive sarvartha sadhike | Sharanye tryambake Gauri Narayani namostute ||"</note>

May there be success in all knowledge.

## Leaf 2 (Bottom)

O Goddess who dwells in the lotus, the pure one, worshipped by everyone, the beloved of Vishnu, I bow to you. O Queen of the Universe, be pleased with me.
<note>original: "Padme padmalaye devi suchite sarva pujite | Vishnupriye namastubhyam praseeda jagadeeshwari ||"</note>

To the most auspicious of all auspicious things, to the one who brings success to all goals, to the protector, the three-eyed one, the golden goddess, to <term>Narayani</term>, I bow to you.

May there be success in all knowledge.

<note>Two circular holes used for binding the cord are visible in the center of each palm leaf.</note>

<summary>This page contains traditional Sanskrit invocations to the goddesses Lakshmi and Saraswati, written in the Grantha-Tamil script. The prayers seek blessings for knowledge, wealth, and success in all endeavors.</summary>

### Top Leaf

To live well in this world, many auspicious matters must be achieved. To make the necessary arrangements for success, one should perform deeds with an auspicious intent on a fortunate and holy day. One should complete these auspicious tasks with the right timing and without delay. These deeds should be carried out in a proper manner, aligned with favorable astrological conjunctions. To finish these auspicious tasks successfully, they must be performed with auspicious conjunctions and in a state of holy blessing.

### Bottom Leaf

One should complete auspicious deeds with discernment. Following the rules and as is appropriate, perform auspicious matters with favorable conjunctions. On a holy and auspicious day, with auspicious intent, one should complete these deeds. Finishing these tasks properly, with the right conjunctions and in a holy manner, is essential. One must complete the auspicious deeds with favorable conjunctions and in a holy, auspicious way.

**तत्सूकपाठस्तु—**

'गायत्र्यै उष्णिगुनुष्टुप् बृहती पङ्क्तिस्त्रिष्टुप् जगत्यै' ॥ १ ॥
गायत्री । उष्णिक् । अनुष्टुप् । बृहती । पङ्क्तिः । त्रिष्टुप् । जगत्यै' ॥ १ ॥

"सप्तसु छन्दःसृचः कल्पयित्वा गायत्र्यादि 'गायत्र्यै स्वाहा' इत्येवं यथाछन्दः" (शांक १८,१) इति तत्रैव शान्तিকল্পे मन्त्राणाम् ऊहनप्रकारस्य दर्शितत्वात् 'गायत्र्यै स्वाहा', 'उष्णिहे स्वाहा', 'अनुष्टुभे स्वाहा', 'पङ्क्त्यै स्वाहा', 'त्रिष्टुभे स्वाहा', 'जगत्यै स्वाहा', इत्येवम् अस्मिन् सूक्ते सप्त मन्त्रा भवन्ति । सर्वे मन्त्राः स्पष्टार्थाः ।

**इति तृतीयेऽनुवाके प्रथमं सूक्तम् ।**

'आङ्गिरसानामाद्यैः' इत्यादिसूक्तद्वयस्य 'आङ्गिरसीं गणकामस्य अभिवरनोऽभिवर्षमाणस्य च' (शांक १७,२) इति विहितायाम् आङ्गिरस्याख्यायां महाशान्तौ विनियोगः । उक्तं हि शान्तিকল্পे— "समासः" (१९,२२:२३) आङ्गिरस्याम् । 'इन्द्र मरुत्व' (अ२,५) इत्येन्द्रयाम्" (शांक १८,१;४) इति । अत्र समासशब्देन एतत् सूक्तद्वयम् उच्यते ।

तत्र 'आङ्गिरसानामाद्यैः' इति सूक्तम् एवम् आम्नायते—

**आङ्गिरसानामाद्यैः पश्वानुवाकैः स्वाहा ॥ १ ॥**
आङ्गिरसानाम् । आद्यैः । पश्व । अनुवाकैः । स्वाहा ॥ १ ॥

**षष्ठाय स्वाहा ॥ २ ॥**
षष्ठाय । स्वाहा ॥ २ ॥

**सप्तमाष्टमाभ्यां स्वाहा ॥ ३ ॥**

गुराज्य: दिवि द्युलोके राजमाना देहिन: शरीरिण: । 'कवचधारणं देहस्यैवेति' देहिनो देवा इत्युक्तम् । ते प्रसिद्धा देवा: तनूषु स्वशरीरेषु यद् वर्म अनहन्त धृतवन्त: । णह बन्धने । कर्त्रभिप्राये क्रियाफले आत्मनेपदम् । असुरयुद्धे स्वदेहरक्षणार्थं प्रतिमुक्तवन्त: । इन्द्र: च यद् वर्म कवचम् चक्रे शत्रुविजयार्थम् । करोते: पूर्ववद् आत्मनेपदम् । तत् कवचं देवैरिनद्रेण च स्वशरीरे धारितम् अस्मान् युद्धोद्यतान् विश्वत: सर्वत: परकृतप्रहारेभ्य: पातु रक्षतु ।

वर्म॑ मे॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी वर्म॑ सूर्य॑: ।
वर्म॑ मे॒ विश्वे॑ दे॒वा: कृ॒ण्वन्तु॒ मा मा॑ प्रा॒पत्प्र॒तीची॑का ॥ ४ ॥

वर्म॑ । मे॒ । द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी इति॑ । वर्म॑ । अह॑: । वर्म॑ । सूर्य॑: ।
वर्म॑ । मे॒ । विश्वे॑ । दे॒वा: । कृ॒ण्वन्तु॑ । मा । मा । प्र । आ॒पत् । प्र॒तीची॑का ॥ ४ ॥

द्यावापृथिवी द्यावापृथिव्यौ मे मम वर्म कवचं कुरुताम् । अह: च वर्म करोतु । सूर्य: च विश्वे सर्वे देवा: इन्द्रादयश्च मे मम युयुत्सोर्मदीयस्य वा राज: वर्म कवचं कृण्वन्तु । करोतेश्छन्दसे लुङि 'मन्त्रे घस' (पा २,४,८०) इति क्लेर्लुक् । झ: सार्वधातुकस्य डित्त्वाद् गुणप्रतिषेधे यण् आदेश: । 'बहुलं छन्दस्यमाङ्योगेऽपि' (पा ६,४,७५) इति अडभाव: । किं च प्रतीचीका प्रत्यगञ्चना प्रतीची । अज्ञातायें कप्रत्यय: । 'केऽण:' (पा ७,४,१३) इति ह्रस्वत्वम् । शत्रुसेना अज्ञानप्रतिकूला सती मा मां कवचधारिणं युध्यन्तं मा मैव प्रापत् प्राप्नोतु । आप्नोतेर्माङि लुङि लुट्त्वाद् अङ् । कवचधारिणो समागत: शत्रुसेना प्रकाशैव आयातु । देवानुगृहीतवचधारणेन हसामपि तां परसेनां हन्तुं शक्नोमीत्यर्थ: ।

इति एकादशं सूक्तम् ।
इति एकोनविंशे काण्डे द्वितीयोनुवाक: ।

तृतीयेऽनुवाके षट् सूक्तानि । तत्र 'गायत्र्युष्णिग्' इति प्रथमसूक्तस्य 'गायत्रीं छन्दोब्रह्मवर्चसकामस्य प्रयुञ्जीत' (शांक १७,२) इति विहितायां गायत्र्याख्यायां महाशान्तौ विनियोग: । उक्तं हि शान्तিকল্পे— 'छन्दोगण: (अ १९,२२) गायत्र्याम्' 'समास:† (अ १९,२२,२३) आग्नेय्याम्' (शांक १८,१) इति ।

<header>Atharva Veda Commentary [Hymn 20, Mantra 4</header>

The gods, who shine in the sky and possess bodies—"the wearing of armor is only for those who have bodies," hence it is said "the gods who have bodies"—they bound that armor onto their own bodies. The root <term>ṇah</term> means to bind. The middle voice is used because the fruit of the action is intended for the doer. They put it on for the sake of protecting their own bodies in the battle against the <term>asuras</term> <gloss>demons</gloss>. And the armor that <term>Indra</term> created for the sake of victory over enemies—the middle voice is used for the root <term>kṛ</term> <gloss>to do/make</gloss> as before. May that armor, worn by the gods and by <term>Indra</term> on their own bodies, protect us, who are ready for battle, from all sides against attacks made by others.

May the heaven and earth be my armor; may the day be my armor; may the sun be my armor. May all the gods make armor for me; may the hostile army never reach me. || 4 ||

May heaven and earth provide armor for me. May the day provide armor. May the sun and all the gods, including <term>Indra</term> and others, make armor for me, for the king or for me who wishes to fight. The root <term>kṛ</term> is used in the Vedic <term>luṅ</term> <gloss>aorist tense</gloss>. "May the hostile army," meaning the enemy force, being counter-intuitive or antagonistic, never reach me, the wearer of this armor. The root <term>āp</term> <gloss>to reach</gloss> is used in the <term>mā-ni</term> <gloss>prohibitive</gloss> mood. The meaning is that the enemy army should only approach the wearer of the armor in the light. Because I am wearing armor favored by the gods, I am able to kill even that enemy army.

Thus ends the eleventh hymn.
Thus ends the second <term>anuvāka</term> of the nineteenth book.

In the third <term>anuvāka</term> there are six hymns. Among them, the first hymn, "The Gayatri, the Ushnih..." is applied in the <term>Mahāśānti</term> <gloss>Great Rite of Pacification</gloss> called "Gayatri," which is prescribed for one who desires <term>brahmavarcas</term> <gloss>radiance of sacred knowledge</gloss>. It is said in the <term>Śāntikalpa</term>: "The group of meters (19.22) in the Gayatri, the collection (19.22:23) in the Agneya."

<summary>The text concludes the armor hymn by invoking heaven, earth, and the gods to protect the warrior, and introduces the ritual application of meters in the Great Rite of Pacification.</summary>

<header>Section 22, Mantra 9] Book Nineteen 1561</header>

**The recitation of that hymn is:**

"To the Gayatri, to the Ushnih, to the Anushtubh, to the Brihati, to the Pankti, to the Trishtubh, to the Jagati." || 1 ||

"Having fashioned the verses into seven meters, such as the Gayatri..."—since the method of changing the mantras in the <term>Śāntikalpa</term> is shown as "To the Gayatri <term>svāhā</term>," "To the Ushnih <term>svāhā</term>," "To the Anushtubh <term>svāhā</term>," "To the Pankti <term>svāhā</term>," "To the Trishtubh <term>svāhā</term>," "To the Jagati <term>svāhā</term>," there are seven mantras in this hymn. All the mantras are clear in meaning.

**Thus ends the first hymn in the third <term>anuvāka</term>.**

The two hymns beginning with "By the first of the Angirasas" are applied in the <term>Mahāśānti</term> called "Angirasi," which is prescribed for one who desires a calculation of the Angirasas and for one who desires to obtain rain or who is experiencing rainfall. It is said in the <term>Śāntikalpa</term>: "The collection (19.22:23) in the Angirasi. 'Indra Marutvan' (2.5) in the Indri." Here, the word "collection" refers to these two hymns.

There, the hymn "By the first of the Angirasas" is recited as follows:

By the first of the Angirasas, five <term>anuvākas</term>; <term>svāhā</term>. || 1 ||

To the sixth; <term>svāhā</term>. || 2 ||

To the seventh and eighth; <term>svāhā</term>. || 3 ||

To the blue-nailed ones; <term>svāhā</term>. || 4 ||

To the green ones; <term>svāhā</term>. || 5 ||

To the small ones; <term>svāhā</term>. || 6 ||

To the sequences; <term>svāhā</term>. || 7 ||

To the first powerful ones; <term>svāhā</term>. || 8 ||

To the second powerful ones; <term>svāhā</term>. || 9 ||

To the third powerful ones; <term>svāhā</term>. || 10 ||

<summary>This page details the liturgical application of various Vedic meters and groups of Angirasa hymns within the Great Rite of Pacification.</summary>

We, the witnesses signed below, gathered for the conflict of acts in language upon confirmation, and like his honor, in the confirmation of the document, for thus below he corrected, to take [it] according to if [he is] like a weight to give him the right. For immediately all of it shall pierce the statute in the document, for he shall give it to him regarding the... for the affairs that are in the customs according to my heart, my servants. And thus from below to the son, in order to... and they established and returned and wrote according to all that passed, so-and-so, from the time of his burden until the time [when] he nears the fruits, regarding the cancellation, in every power and strength, to bear, he will let be... the affairs of so-and-so, we bring from his writing according to his acquisitions, and those from [the hand of]... for the gathering, the fine, and they were punished. So-and-so acquired in our presence, our son, as in all power and strength that is for the... to his name, in general, for the salvation, he established [and] corrected in the world in every use, he will teach the palm as if [in] exile, for this matter, this [is] in the weighing, tamar [date/palm], and judgments to give him monies in every place [that] he will strengthen, and also in our repetition in the exchange, in all the foundation of so-and-so...

Why is it necessary to have it from without and from within? It is because the upper union is constant for the Crown <term>Atarah</term> <gloss>the Sefirah of Malchut</gloss> which is influenced by the Holy of Holies at every time they need it. The secret of the Crown is that <term>Tiferet</term> and <term>Malchut</term>, the two ends, enter into the rooms of the actual Kingship. The Kings will spread out into Understanding <term>Binah</term> and there will be different fruits from the servant Jacob and Rachel so that they may take the crown in number. 

The numerical value of Kingship <term>Malchut</term> itself is 40 and 70. Know that the "Small Face" <term>Zeir Anpin</term> <gloss>the six Sefirot from Chesed to Yesod</gloss> is known as "two crowns." One is from without, which is before the <term>Chesed</term> <gloss>Loving-kindness</gloss> of the mother, and one is from the hidden Understanding <term>Binah</term>. It was entirely for itself, and the Blessed One gave a portion of His glory to the female forever. These crowns are the two aspects written. 

Do not let it enter your mind that there is any death in the place of judgments. The "Small Face" is the master of the aspects and the worker of the sweetening. For he prepares the daughters as heirs and arranges the waters in the heart of the heart to provide for the daughter, to include her in mercies. In the secret of the worker of the "tithe of the wise," he removes the accusations from her. 

Know that there is no pair of <term>Tiferet</term> and <term>Malchut</term> except when they are aroused. There are eighty branches. <term>Chesed</term> is the branch for the future, like the aspect of reaching the prayer shawl. This occurs day by day. And so in the nature of everything, it is covered in the morning. This happens four times, specifically in the portion of <term>Bereshit</term> <gloss>Genesis</gloss>, according to the reason of the creation of man. Outside of this, they are "two countenances" back-to-back, and at the time it is written that "the Lord did not save," it means the "Small Face" included right and left over the earth. 

He reigned in his place and they dreamed of passing through it. He passed through them to preserve the bodies. Man should not cling to it except in the aspect of "face to face." Therefore, there is no foundation <term>Yesod</term> below in this world, nor above in <term>Tiferet</term> and <term>Malchut</term>. They do not need to ascend to be in the palace of Understanding <term>Binah</term>. 

The branches from <term>Tiferet</term> and <term>Malchut</term> are the six edges. You already know that the letters themselves do not have the sanctity of the Name on their own, except through the matter of <term>Tiferet</term> and <term>Malchut</term>. They have the power to unite in a holy union to prepare the souls for them. Whatever they do not have is from above. When they work to unite in the upper palace, it is the mystery of the letters <term>Yod-He-Vav-He</term>. Those who sanctify themselves understand that the Name is also in the sanctity of the Name. 

However, in the power of <term>Tiferet</term> and <term>Malchut</term> they are established above face to face. Since they were not in their place, the essence of the building was in the wall, as it was said when it is called "the one who supports." He also had help and assistance, which is the letter <term>Samekh</term>, until the mixing of everything. This hints at the male who supports. In the intention of the lower garments, the source of the abundance was opened for them from <term>Tiferet</term> through their souls. It returns to the back from the garment to its source. This is the way of the Kingship, according to the spiritual secret that increases. It stands opposite the husband, for she receives more. They are prepared in their place in the presence of your Master and they do not bless unless they are sanctified by the Name. Thus, a man and his wife among the lower ones are a hint to the letters <term>Vav</term> and <term>He</term>. Their blessing is through their labor, and their intention is toward <term>Tiferet</term> and the community of Israel.

Upon the world, like a righteous man in his dwelling, and in his daughter in the creation and her host, everything precedes the coming of the singular and unique one. The place is assigned to her, and the word is alone, influenced but not influencing. To grasp the light, they needed to ascend to them. And the secret of the daughter is a path of water that includes the designated time of the Kingship <term>Malchut</term>. 

The secret of the sign of the covenant <note>the Sefirah of Yesod</note> is that it is the foundation <term>Yesod</term>, for it only influences the aura of the world from the source of life. The navel is designated from the joints and the flowing waters from within the well. It was not said that they flowed from the eye, but from the foundation, which is like a curtain drawn from the source. Therefore, it said "flowing" and "subduing." Those who are sweetened by the judgments in the secular world return and repeat the light in the secrets of the hands that encompass the one who is balanced. It is wrapped in the light of the day, as it is said: "He cuts the waters by His mouth." This means the flowing waters are after the source of <term>Tiferet</term> and it is in the middle of the path. One who prepares the right side digs the pit of the soul. For Abraham to dig them, the Philistines hid them. 

The entire Chariot <note>the divine structure</note> is found to be hinted at in this, according to the secret of the Sefirot. There is here the secret of the eye that looks at the Holy One, Blessed be He, with the names of the unique ones. This refers to their roots above, for in the internal waters from the resting place, this is the secret of the descent. For God's blessing is upon the fountain in the secret of "he will see from the look." He establishes himself like an embrace of the right side, as it is written: "his right hand embraces me." This is in order to be included in the secret of the influence and the speech from above, in the secret of the upper beard that sweetens the male waters for the Kingship. In the right side is the secret for those below. Thus, these are the two righteous ones and the judgments. 

The female aspect is the answer of the roses. The image of Jacob is carved below. Although he was small, he was similar to the image on the Throne. It was like the image in the windows. Furthermore, all the righteous ones whose goodness is in Understanding <term>Binah</term> do not lose anything. Their teachings are also found there. This means they do not diminish in their goodness but are hidden for the future. If they were not sunken in goodness, they would be visible as stars in the days of the Messiah. See the book "The Language of Truth" regarding the building of David, King of Israel. 

Jacob is superior to all of them, for in that place he is called "the house" and not just "branches." There are further reasons in the wisdom of the soul to bring it together with the souls of the righteous, whether in the world of the infants or the world of the great. For in the vision of the world, all of them are the dwelling place of the Holy One, Blessed be He, in the body. As it is written in the portion of <term>Lech Lecha</term> <gloss>page 82</gloss>, all is one and there is no change of countenance. The qualities of the Torah are also present when the Holy One, Blessed be He, releases one from punishment. 

Regarding the soul that ascends above, it is a union and a meeting to receive the blessing like the upper fountain. Torah is never forgotten from the lower ones, and it is prepared for the end of time to assist. There is a reason for the countenances of the constant and the arrangement of the two breads upon the table, the bread of the Presence. For whom is it prepared? For the father at the start of the meal. The bread is for the blessing of the sustenance, fixed as three and three until one hundred. So too is the order of the offerings according to the secret of the meal as we have studied.
